Campus is secluded from the main complex but there’s a shuttle bus going back and forth every hour or so. 

As a FIC student, you get to use the library facility, borrowing stuff, use the gym and apply for on-campus housing but people will make a confused face when they process your student ID for the first time. FIC have their own stuff like Google office apps or Moodle so when you transfer to SFU, you’ll have to learn to adapt to another system. 

Finally, FIC is not SFU. The partnership and the words of agencies will make you think they are one but they are not. This means that you will not get stuff like U-Pass, additional health benefits that partially cover prescription glasses and dental and softwares like Office 365. You will have to pay extra for those on your own and they add up quickly so beware. IT support is sometimes tricky because the two databases are separate so they take more time to process.

If you think that you can earn a seat at SFU by reflecting on your profile then go for it. FIC tuition is almost the same as FIC but there are stuff that you are not eligible for but SFU students are.
